transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-15 14:00 PDT; Duration: ~58 minutes; Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Romero (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Alan Reyes (Acme Security), Priya Singh (Acme Compliance), Tom Brooks (CTO), Sara Lowe (DevOps), Michael Grant (Legal)

[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We do a quick roll call? I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Maya SE, Luis Solutions on for architecture.
[00:12] Alan: Alan here from security. Priya compliance, Tom CTO, Sara DevOps, Michael legal.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. The purpose today is a security and data handling review — specifically prompt retention, PII/PHI concerns, and the standard "no training on customer data" confirmation. We'll run through SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO flows, logging and retention, encryption/KMS, and private deployment options. Sound good?
[00:36] Priya: Yes, that's exactly what we want. We also want to confirm contractual language around data not being used to train models.
[00:42] Maya: Totally. We'll also show how Dedicated and Private deployments work for data residency. Quick note, transcription may mis-hear a few product names — apologies in advance.

[01:05] Jordan: To start, on certifications: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we also have ISO 27001 compliance summary — I can share the reports. They cover our control environment, change management, and incident response.
[01:23] Alan: Do you have a SOC 2 report we can share under NDA? Acme requires the full Type II for vendors with elevated access.
[01:30] Jordan: Yes, we'll send the Type II report via our secure portal. I'll add the ISO summary as well. Action item there.

[02:05] Maya: On identity — we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, plus SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based: you can map your IdP groups to Redwood roles (Admin, Operator, Viewer). For Dedicated/Private we can also integrate with your on-prem AD via SAML.
[02:28] Sara: For SCIM provisioning, can we sync groups for fine-grained RBAC? We need to make sure access to production models is limited.
[02:36] Maya: Yes, SCIM supports group sync; you can lock down routes and model versions by role. Logs capture role changes.

[03:10] Tom: Audit logs — what's the retention window by default and can we export to our SIEM?
[03:16] Luis: Default audit log retention for hosted is 90 days for activity logs and 30 days for full transcripts, but you can configure shorter retention. We provide integrations for streaming logs to S3, Splunk, Datadog, or your SIEM. For Dedicated/Private you can set retention to zero or keep logs within your VPC.
[03:38] Priya: Wait — transcripts? Are you saying full prompt/response bodies are retained? We need to understand what's retained and for how long and how to opt-out.
[03:47] Maya: Right. For the hosted API default, the platform keeps request/response payloads for up to 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. But we have contractual and config controls: you can opt into zero retention for prompt and completions, and you can also disable analytics ingestion. For workloads with PHI, we recommend Dedicated or Private with zero retention and customer-managed keys.
[04:10] Alan: Is zero retention an account-level setting or per-route?
[04:13] Luis: It's per-project/route configurable for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have an account-level 'no retention' flag we can enable during onboarding, but it's gated by contract. We'll include the exact flag name in the docs.

[04:55] Jordan: Important point on training: Redwood does not use customer prompt or content to train or improve public models. We can confirm that in contract language — "no training on customer data". For hosted customers, aggregated telemetry may be used for product metrics unless disabled by the no-telemetry flag.
[05:16] Michael: We need explicit contractual language stating customer content is never used to train models, and that Redwood will not derive feature improvements from customer PII.
[05:24] Jordan: Understood — we'll provide suggested clause language and are open to negotiation. We also provide a data processing addendum (DPA) that includes processing purposes and retention.

[06:05] Priya: Regarding PII and PHI — can you confirm whether Redwood does any redaction or scanning by default? We have to know if any PHI will leave our environment.
[06:16] Maya: We do offer optional PII detection tooling, but it's an opt-in feature. By default, we don't modify customer payloads. For PHI workloads, best practice is to use Private or Dedicated with customer-managed encryption keys and disable retention and analytics.
[06:33] Sara: For Dedicated, does data ever leave our VPC?
[06:36] Luis: For Redwood Private, the control plane can be run in Redwood's managed mode or self-hosted; in self-hosted/on-prem options, data never leaves your network. For Dedicated, it's isolated GPU pools but still a Redwood-managed environment — there are options for network peering and strict egress rules. We'll detail the exact network flows.
[06:58] Tom: Encryption — do you support customer-managed KMS (HSM) for model keys and logs?
[07:04] Maya: Yes, we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS. You can use customer-managed keys for data at rest and for keys used to encrypt logs. For further assurance we can discuss HSM-backed keys for the most sensitive customers.
[07:20] Alan: Can we rotate keys and have key rotation logs forwarded to our audit?
[07:25] Luis: Key rotation can be done from your side and we surface rotation events in the audit logs. We'll also provide a key-usage report for the pilot.

[08:00] Jordan: On lineage and traceability — every request has an ID, user ID, and route; we can provide trace logs and link them to audit events. For tamper evidence, we provide log signing options and append-only export to customer S3 with integrity checks.
[08:20] Priya: That helps. For regulatory reasons, we need to be able to produce logs for audits and show who accessed what prompts and when.
[08:29] Maya: You can retain full audit chains; for Private setups, we can configure indefinite retention in your storage. For hosted we typically keep them per retention policy but you can export to your SIEM for long-term retention.

[09:10] Alan: About the 'no training' line again — how do you technically enforce that? Is there a governance mechanism?
[09:17] Jordan: We have internal controls that prevent customer prompt/response data from entering model training pipelines. It’s enforced by policy and implemented by separating telemetry and model training datasets. We can provide an architecture note showing the data flows and the logical separation — will share with Maya's diagram.
[09:36] Michael: We'll want proof points — e.g., logs or attestations showing process separation.
[09:41] Jordan: We'll include that in the SOC 2 documentation and the DPA.

[10:05] Sara: Can we run a small scale test where we send synthetic PHI and verify retention is disabled and logs are only stored in our S3?
[10:11] Maya: Yes, that's part of the pilot scope — we'll provision a Dedicated environment with the no-retention flag and output logs to your S3. We'll coordinate with your DevOps.

[12:00] [Longer technical dive — Maya shares high-level architecture]
[12:03] Maya: (describing) On inbound requests we terminate TLS at the edge, we route by policy to model runtime. For Dedicated we have dedicated GPU pools; KV cache and prefix caching are within the runtime. For Private self-hosted, all runtime and storage can be inside your environment. The control plane in managed Private mode only holds orchestration metadata and not the content — and we can run the control plane in your VPC if needed.
[12:35] Tom: Is the control plane metadata sensitive?
[12:38] Maya: It depends; metadata includes model versions, route configs, and billing metadata — we can minimize what's stored and you can opt for a customer-controlled control plane.

[15:00] Alan: A question about backups — are backups encrypted with customer keys? Who has access to backup data?
[15:07] Luis: Backups are encrypted at rest. For Private/self-hosted, backups are under your control and use your KMS. For hosted/Dedicated we can also configure BYOK for backups. Access to backups is restricted to operations with strict RBAC and is audited.

[18:10] Priya: For regulatory audits, we need to know retention deletion guarantees — if we say delete data after X days, how do we prove deletion?
[18:20] Maya: We provide deletion APIs and deletion logs. For complete forensic proof, we offer a deletion certificate exported to your SIEM and an internal process trace. For the highest assurance, run Private with storage under your control.

[21:00] Jordan: Regarding telemetry and aggregated metrics — we do collect non-content telemetry by default for product improvements, but that can be entirely disabled. When disabled, we still retain billing-relevant metadata for reconciliation.
[21:20] Priya: Billing reconciliation — what minimal metadata is required for invoicing?
[21:25] Jordan: Typically usage aggregates (tokens per project) and request counts. We can provide aggregated invoices without storing content-level records.

[24:30] Michael: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a list for our vendor risk program.
[24:37] Jordan: We maintain a subprocessors list and will provide the latest vendor list; common ones include cloud providers, monitoring vendors, and analytics providers — but you can opt out of analytics integrations.

[27:10] Alan: How about incidents and breach notification timeframes?
[27:16] Luis: Our incident response SLA: initial notification within 72 hours for security incidents; severity-based escalations. SOC 2 covers our IR processes.

[30:00] Priya: Data residency — we need US-only for production data, EU for EU customers. Can you pin regions?
[30:08] Maya: Yes — regional pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have region selection and can route requests to specific regions with data residency controls. We'll include a mapping of available regions.

[33:10] Sara: For the pilot, we want daily deletion of transcripts and immediate forwarding of logs to S3. Is that doable?
[33:18] Luis: Yes, we'll set retention to 1 day for hosted pilot or zero for Dedicated, and configure log forwarding to your S3. We'll include a runbook for the setup.

[36:00] Tom: Any downside if we disable retention entirely? For example, will debugging or rate-limit investigations be harder?
[36:10] Maya: Debugging becomes harder without payloads; we can keep structured metadata for debugging without storing full text. We can also implement ephemeral debug snapshots under strict access control that auto-delete after a short window.

[40:00] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll send SOC 2 and ISO docs, provide architecture diagram and key management notes, propose contractual no-training clause and DPA edits, and scope a Dedicated pilot with zero retention and S3 export.
[40:18] Priya: That covers our major concerns. One last question — do you have customers in healthcare using Redwood for PHI? Any case studies or references?
[40:27] Jordan: We have several healthcare customers on Dedicated/Private. We can provide redacted reference statements under NDA.

[42:45] Michael: Legal needs the proposed no-training language. Can you draft something that says: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train models or improve model weights, and will not incorporate Customer Data into any model training or feature engineering process, directly or indirectly" — and include carve-outs for aggregated telemetry if agreed.
[43:02] Jordan: Yes, we'll propose that wording and include options for telem opt-out.

[45:00] Maya: Technical note — for PHI we recommend: Dedicated/Private, BYOK, zero retention, SAML for SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and export to customer SIEM/S3. We will also enable log signing if desired.

[47:30] Alan: One more: Are your employees allowed to access raw prompts by default? How are internal approvals handled?
[47:36] Luis: Access is strictly RBAC-limited; there's an internal process with approvals and audit. Support engineers may have elevated access for debugging but only with explicit customer opt-in and under documented process; we can make support access an opt-in that requires explicit ticket and justification.

[50:00] Jordan: We should plan for a quick dry-run of the contract clause and a pilot checklist. Also we'll supply the subprocessor list and incident response playbook.
[50:10] Priya: Sounds good. We'll review and come back with any follow-up.

[55:00] Tom: Thanks everyone. We'll expect the docs and pilot plan in the next week.
[55:06] Jordan: Thanks — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had minor mis-hearings (e.g., K V cache shown as K V cache, Redwood Dedicated sometimes parsed as red wood dedicated), some speaker overlaps and filler words removed for brevity.
